- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon) — adjust downward bias for short-term outlooks.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ → 60s) — reduce forecast peak values by 5–15% to avoid overshoot.
- Shows mean reversion bias — forecasts tend to overcorrect toward lower values after high peaks; add slight upward momentum correction.
- Lagged response to recent history — model reacts too slowly to recent price drops; increase sensitivity to last 7–10 days.
- Overly optimistic in mid-forecast horizon (days 10–20) — reduce forecast values by 2–5% for this window to align with observed volatility decay.
- Underestimates in late forecast (days 20–30) — add 3–5% upward adjustment to compensate for persistent downward pressure or market stabilization.
